title: Some Questions Concerning Methods of Leadership
author: Mao Zedong
context: Written in June 1943 during the Yan'an Rectification Movement, this resolution formulated the Marxist theory of leadership and the mass line: 'from the masses, to the masses' and combining the general call with particular guidance.
relatesToToday: Essential for socialist organizing and democratic accountability, demonstrating how leadership must avoid both bureaucratic commandism and tailism by synthesizing the concrete experiences of working people.
keyTakeaways: All correct leadership must be 'from the masses, to the masses', systematically concentrating the scattered ideas of the masses and testing them in practical action.
Effective leadership requires combining general calls with particular, concrete guidance in specific units to prevent empty bureaucracy.
A unified leading group must be linked with the active masses and continually renewed through actual struggle.
